description: Long low hall with an open colonnaded front sheltering a gilded Buddha figure lying on its side, the figure visible the length of the opening.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Long low rectangular hall under a shallow two-tier tiled roof, one long side open as a colonnade of square pillars with no wall between them, a very long gilded Buddha figure lying on its side on a low plinth running the full interior length, head propped on one hand at the near end and feet squared off at the far end, low stepped platform along the open front Materials: Gold-leafed figure with worn patches showing dark lacquer beneath, red and gold roof tiles, whitewashed pillars stained at the base, dusty stone plinth, soot darkening on the ceiling above.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.86, up from 0.79, and the whole of the gain is that this prop finally HAS a proxy. Meshy still refuses the plate (content_policy_violation, safety checker forced on), but fal-ai/trellis and fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2 both accept it, and two independent reconstructions agreeing is better evidence than one Meshy mesh. They put length/height at 1.852 and 2.020 against the build's 2.818 -- the hall was 46% too long -- and width/height at 1.226 and 1.265 against 1.410. Corrected to 12.38 x 10.00 x 19.24 m, the band table goes from mean |delta depth| 0.7267 to 0.0789 and |delta width| 0.1312 to 0.0739, with the bands over the 0.12 flag dropping from ten of ten to two. The roof was also the WRONG FORM: a gable, where the plate and both proxies show a hip. The remaining drag is materialSurface 0.82 and lightingCamera 0.80, and neither has an evidence-backed fix -- the plate is the darkest in the kit and its subject sits in its own shade, and a tile texture is exactly the opt-in the textureless default exists to refuse at prop distance. 2,892/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: A 15.1 m figure on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, head at +Z: one smooth body from neck to ankle, taller than deep, the upper leg a soft ridge on it, stacked feet with a toe comb, an upright tilted head with ushnisha and ear lobes cupped in the right hand, the forearm near-vertical from an elbow on the plinth, the left arm along the flank to a hand on the thigh.
featureReviews.notes: The only organic form in the kit, and it needed a shape helper written for it alone: a reclining body is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it, and a box decomposition of that is not a low-poly body but a pile of luggage. Every station's centre height is DERIVED from its own radius -- cy = plinth top + ry, computed rather than authored -- which is the only way a varying section can rest on a flat plinth at every point. The first promoted build was ONE symmetric tube from head to feet with the head at -Z, and it read as a figure on its back facing the wall; the rebuild carries the asymmetry that says on-its-side. Two earlier pose faults were found by review rather than by a gate: the arm ran too high and too far and covered the head entirely from the +X side, which is the only side anyone sees this prop from, and the ushnisha wanted 0.70 m of height where the soffit leaves 0.50. Reproportioned with the hall: it keeps the hall's own z scale and THICKENS -- 22.04 m of head-to-toe extent to 15.14 m and the section from 2.80 to 3.08 m, so length/depth goes 7.2 -> 4.9, which is what a human lying on its side actually measures and 7.2 is a pipe. The factor must be SZ and not something chosen to fill the hall: the figure does not sit in the hall, it sits on the PLINTH, which is scaled by SZ, and one build at 0.79 put the feet 1.1 m past the end of their own plinth and out through the end colonnade.

featureReviews.evidence: Twelve columns leaving the whole long front open, with the figure legible through them along its length and a dark interior face at luma 82 behind.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes require this and give the reason: a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and reads as a warehouse. The interior shade fills the gaps between twelve columns, so its luma margin over the backdrop's 58 matters more here than anywhere -- at the backdrop value the gate would read eleven separate holes through the building. Its two panels also had to drop from 6.60 to 6.54: at the column head height each shared that plane with every column, and because the columns are an InstancedMesh, check-coplanar reported one mistake as twelve pairs.

featureReviews.evidence: Two HIPPED tiers at pitch 0.64 -- about 33 degrees -- sloping in on all four sides from eaves at 6.60 to a ridge at 9.68, each tier carrying an ochre eaves course under a red tile field, a capped rib down every one of its four hips and a capped ridge; the upper tier's eaves overhang the lower roof's surface by 0.25 m to make the double eave.
featureReviews.notes: This was a GABLE and it was the largest single error on the prop. Cropping the plate's roof out settles it in one look -- both tiers slope in at the ends, every corner wears a white-grey capped diagonal rib, and the ridge is a short capped line well inside the eaves -- and both proxies agree: the reference end elevation narrows steadily from eaves to ridge, which a gable cannot do. Built now through the preamble's hipRoof at curveExp 1, a straight Thai hip rather than a temple sweep, with ridgeHalfZ = hz - hx so the pitch is equal along both axes -- which is what a hip IS -- and y1 derived as y0 + pitch * hx so the pitch stays the one that was measured. Two cones per tier carry the banding: the gold cone is the whole tier, the red field starts one band up and stands 40 mm PROUD, because flush they would be coincident co-facing surfaces over the whole roof and inset the red would never be seen. The ribs are chained along hipRoof's own parametrisation, not aimed straight: the helper flares its eaves ring by 1 + 0.045 across the lower third whether or not cornerLift is zero, so the hip bows and a straight box cuts the chord and lifts off the surface at the eaves. The old bargeboard rake-angle bug -- atan(pitch) where atan2(run, rise) was wanted -- is gone with the bargeboards, which were rake boards for a form this prop does not have.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials at PBR confidence 0.822-0.860, four measured on lit faces and the fifth corrected with its reasoning recorded.
featureReviews.notes: The gilt is the largest deliberate deviation on the prop. The figure is the ONE surface in this plate that is never directly lit -- deep shade, behind columns, under a soffit -- so its mean across 41,296 warm-hued pixels, #7D6040, is illumination and not albedo, and renders the figure brown. The albedo taken is the brightest QUARTILE of those pixels, #AC8E6F, which is the same 'measure a lit face' rule applied to a surface that has no lit face; the brightest 8% at #BEA07E was tried first and rendered cream. It ships at #AC7741: that hue and value kept exactly, chroma raised from 0.36 to 0.62, with metalness halved to 0.15 because a metal with no environment map has its diffuse scaled by (1-metalness) and drains the chroma out of exactly the surface that has to read as gold.

name: Reclining Buddha Hall
nameTh: วิหารพระนอน
notes:
The reclining figure is modelled as part of this asset rather than as a separate statue, and the long front is open colonnade rather than a wall, because the two decisions depend on each other: a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and would read as a warehouse, and the whole identity of the building is the gilded figure seen lengthwise through the opening. That means this asset is a building and a large statue together and its material budget has to cover both gold leaf and roofing. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.

SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from 14.0 x 10.0 x 28.0. The 28 m was a list-time estimate reasoned from the figure ('the figure alone sets the minimum length') and never checked, because Meshy refuses this plate with a content_policy_violation and the safety checker is forced on -- so this was the only prop in the kit whose proportions had never been checked band by band, and its silhouette layer was carried at 0.72 for exactly that reason. Meshy is not the only image-to-3d: fal-ai/trellis and fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2 both accept the plate. They read length/height 1.852 and 2.020 and width/height 1.226 and 1.265 -- agreeing with each other to 8.7% and 3.2%, and disagreeing with the build's 2.818 and 1.410 by 46% and 13%. Height is the anchor and does not move: the proxies give ratios only, and the vertical breakdown was already right (the proxy end elevation puts the roof at 31% of total height against the build's 32%). At h 10.0 the mean gives d 19.24 and w 12.38. The band table then goes from mean |delta depth| 0.7267 to 0.0789 and |delta width| 0.1312 to 0.0739.

The plate cannot arbitrate this, and that is measured rather than assumed: a projective solve needs edges that are parallel in plan to be parallel in the image, and fitting the platform's ground silhouette gives four clean straight runs whose two must-be-parallel pairs differ in image slope by 47% and 34%. No single camera projects that -- the plate is a generated image and its perspective is only locally consistent. Do not re-attempt the solve here. The known proxy bias runs with the correction rather than against it: single-view reconstructions inflate depth, so if these two are wrong the true hall is shorter still, and 19.24 m is a floor.
